content_html_sanitized:
Posted February 14, 2001
(MarijuanaNews note: Like California’s Prop 215, but unlike the Soros-sponsored Americans for Medical Rights initiatives, the Utah medical marijuana law would not have any arbitrary limit on the number of plants a patient or supplier can have. Yes, there is a provision for supply! This is very encouraging.

Moreover, their arguments include references to the Constitution that will appeal to Utah conservatives, who – unlike their Senator Orrin Hatch – actually believe in freedom.

I am also pleased that they anticipate some of the prohibitionist arguments in their press release. Bravo!)

The 21st Amendment gives exclusive authority to the states to regulate intoxicating liquors. There is no authorization in the Constitution for the federal government to over-ride the will of the people of Utah regarding medical marijuana. "

" We realize that the American public seems more receptive to marijuana law reform today than it has in many years ", explains Larsen. " A strong majority has supported the legal availability of medical marijuana at least since 1995, when a poll commissioned by the ACLU revealed that 79 percent of the public said they thought it " would be a good idea to legalize marijuana to relieve pain and for other medical uses if prescribed by a doctor. "

Today, at least 24 professional medical associations, including the American Medical Association, the American Public Health Association, and the New England Journal of Medicine publicly support access to Cannabis upon a physician's advice or recommendation.
(MarijuanaNews note: They have overstated the AMA position, which – alas – is not that courageous. stated an American Medical Association December 1997 report that called on federal officials to encourage well-controlled human studies, saying " Anecdotal, survey, and clinical data support the view that smoked marijuana ... provide[s] symptomatic relief in some patients. " )

" I have personally conducted animal studies on a drug called CT-3, a cannabinoid with great promise and potential to relieve arthritis pain, without stomach ulceration ", concludes Larsen. " The only things keeping it from the hands of the suffering are archaic and compassionless laws. Let's be reasonable and allow the sick to choose their medicine. "

# # #
(MarijuanaNews note: The press release ends with this quote.)
" In strict medical terms marijuana is far safer than many foods we commonly consume. It is physically impossible to eat enough marijuana to induce death. Marijuana, in its natural form, is one of the safest therapeutically active substances known to man. "
Francis L. Young Administrative Law Judge of the US drug police DEA September 6, 1988

(MarijuanaNews note: The text of the proposed initiative follows.)

The Utah State Code shall be amended to include the following:

Be it enacted by the people of Utah:

  1. Any previous law notwithstanding, licensed medical practitioners with authority to issue pharmaceutical prescriptions shall not be prosecuted for issuing prescriptions for Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) or any other cannabinoid or cannabinoid-containing substance for medical use.

  2. Any previous law notwithstanding, persons with current medical prescriptions from a licensed medical practitioner for THC or any other cannabinoid or cannabinoid-containing substance for medical use, shall not be prosecuted for possession or personal use of any amount of THC or other cannabinoid or cannabinoid-containing substance.

  3. Any previous law notwithstanding, no person shall be prosecuted for producing, possessing or distributing solely to persons with current medical prescriptions for the same, any amount of THC or other cannabinoid or cannabinoid-containing substance.
